_comment: Cross-platform contract for builder-paywall decoding + text/variable semantics. The TS authoring schema is STRICT (unknown node types are rejected: acceptLenient entries FAIL it). Platform decoders (Swift Codable, Kotlin kotlinx-serialization) are lenient by design: unknown node types decode to an unknown node retaining id+fallback and render the fallback (or nothing); an override entry with an unknown `when.kind` is skipped individually (that one entry ignored, config otherwise decodes normally) — also acceptLenient, per the unknown-condition-kind leniency rule (spec D2/D3). A countdown carrying BOTH `endsAt` and `durationSeconds` is acceptLenient for the same reason: the exclusivity is a TS-only `.refine` (authoring-time), while the native decoders take it and must then PREFER `endsAt` — that preference is the contract, not the rejection. reject entries must fail EVERYWHERE (schema AND platform decoders → null), including a structural key (e.g. `type`) inside override props on an otherwise-KNOWN when.kind — malformed props in a known kind is a whole-config failure, not a skippable entry. Overrides APPLICATION semantics (base props, then matching overrides in array order, later wins, shallow per-field) are pinned by per-platform unit tests sharing D-Task 1's TS case table (schema.test.ts / validate.test.ts `applyOverrides` cases) — NOT by fixture sections here, since applying overrides needs live selected/introEligible state the static fixture format doesn't carry. Generated from the real TS implementations; frozen — regenerate only by re-running the generator against packages/shared/src/paywall. VISIBILITY vectors (`visibility` section) pin EVALUATION, not just decoding: each case is {visibility, platform, appVersion} -> expected boolean, and the TS `isNodeVisible` is proven against them here. The three `accept` entries only prove a decoder PARSES the key — they go green even on a decoder that drops `visibility` entirely — so stage 2's SwiftUI/Kotlin visibility MUST be driven by this vector table (mirror the `variables`/`resolveText` pattern), not by the accept entries. The load-bearing rules a naive decoder gets wrong: component-wise digit comparison (1.10 > 1.9, 1.2 == 1.2.0), inclusive bounds, and FAIL OPEN on unknown platform / unknown version / non-numeric component — the last of which must not throw when splitting on '.'. React Native renders through the native views as of 2026-07-25 and is no longer an independent decoder.

accept.name: canonical every-node multi-locale
three-level nested stacks with z overlay
node carrying a valid fallback
theme pair without dark
explicit packageIds with defaultSelected
url and restore buttons, spacer flexible
duplicate sibling node ids (schema-legal: uniqueness is a validator concern, not a schema one; renderers must decode and render without crashing — keyed positionally, never by id)
overrides: introEligible + selected across node types, incl. a text key-swap
overrides: packageList (empty props) + purchaseButton labelKey swap, selected outside any cellTemplate
packageList with cellTemplate (visual nodes only, selected-condition badge)
visibility — platform-scoped node
accept._note: Every decoder must parse `visibility.platform` and render the node only on the listed platforms. An absent or EMPTY list means all platforms.

accept.name: visibility — both app-version bounds
accept._note: Bounds are INCLUSIVE and compared component-wise on digits, not as semver. An unknown app version, or a component that is not a run of digits, must FAIL OPEN — render the node.

accept.name: visibility — empty object means no constraint
accept._note: `visibility: {}` must decode and behave exactly like an absent key: the node renders everywhere.

accept.name: divider: explicit color/thickness/inset, and a bare default-styled hairline
icon: explicit size/color, and a bare default-size uncolored icon
featureList: multi-row with a mix of included values
timeline: rows with and without captions
socialProof: with a fractional rating
socialProof: without a rating (no stars)
purchaseButton with trialLabelKey (both keys present in default locale)
stickyFooter: pinned footer with a nested purchaseButton
countdown: absolute deadline with a label and onExpiry
stickyFooter: bare footer, every optional prop absent (no background -> STICKY_FOOTER_DEFAULT_BACKGROUND, substituted not inherited)
countdown: durationSeconds anchor with onExpiry hide (no endsAt; deadline = persisted first-shown anchor + durationSeconds)
countdown: bare node, every optional prop absent (onExpiry -> COUNTDOWN_DEFAULT_ON_EXPIRY freeze, no label, no colour instruction -> ambient ink)
carousel-bare
carousel-full
video-bare
video-full
lottie-bare
lottie-full
stack: border drawn inside its cornerRadius (node style pass)
text: badge via background + cornerRadius (node style pass)
button: custom background/labelColor/border/cornerRadius overriding its style variant (node style pass)
purchaseButton: custom background/labelColor/border/cornerRadius (node style pass)

acceptLenient.name: countdown carrying BOTH endsAt and durationSeconds (strict schema rejects the exclusivity refine; platform decoders decode it and MUST prefer endsAt)
unknown node type with valid fallback (platform decoders keep id+fallback; strict schema rejects)
unknown node type without fallback (platforms render nothing)
override with unknown when.kind 'sizeClass' (strict schema rejects the whole config; platform decoders decode leniently, skipping ONLY this override entry per the unknown-condition-kind rule)
unknown node type carrying visibility (decoders MUST retain it)
acceptLenient._note: visibility is the author's 'don't show this here'. An unknown type is exactly the forward-compat case where that matters most: dropping it renders the fallback on a platform the author excluded. The web renderer gates before it ever reaches the unknown branch, so the three native decoders must retain visibility on their unknown node too.

reject.name: non-object localization value
reject.reason: localizations values must be string tables

reject.name: root is not a stack
reject.reason: root must be a stack node

reject.name: structural key 'type' inside override props on a known when.kind
reject.reason: malformed props in a known kind: 'type' is a structural field, never overridable — strict schema rejects, and platform decoders must ALSO fail the whole config (not just skip the entry, since introEligible IS a known kind)

visibility.name: empty platform list means all
visibility._note: An empty array is NOT 'nowhere' — it is 'no constraint'.

visibility.name: component-wise, not lexical: 1.10 > 1.9
visibility._note: 1.9.0 is BELOW 1.10.0 — decoders splitting on '.' and comparing strings get this wrong.

visibility.name: unknown app version fails open, both bounds
non-numeric component is inconclusive -> fail open
visibility._note: A component that is not a run of digits makes the comparison inconclusive; inconclusive fails OPEN. `"1.0.0-beta".split('.').map(Int)` MUST NOT throw the decoder.

visibility.name: blank platform string is UNKNOWN, not a mismatch -> fail open
visibility._note: TS's own types forbid this input (VisibilityPlatform | null), but the native ports take a nullable String, so "" is reachable there. The TS reference fails open on it via JS falsiness; Kotlin and Swift must agree rather than hiding the node.

trialLabel._comment: expectedKey = which loc key the CTA renders. selectedHasIntroPeriod mirrors PackageView.introPeriod non-empty.

cases.name: no trial falls back to labelKey
no selection is not a trial
